subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: After fixing system-only suffix preservation, should DeepSeek cache compatibility remain a public `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache` option with an automatic default, or become an internal provider capability?
rationale: The cache improvement is proven, but adding a long-lived config surface and moving system-owned context into user-role content establish product and API contracts that require maintainer intent.

options.title: Internal provider capability
options.body: Keep the DeepSeek-specific behavior in provider or catalog metadata and avoid another public option unless a supported operator opt-out is required.

options.title: Public compat option
options.body: Retain the option and default with explicit upgrade, role-semantic, and false-opt-out documentation and tests.

options.title: Generic config-free rule
options.body: Apply a broader implicit-prefix-cache rule only after equivalent semantic and live proof for sibling providers.

recommendation.title: Internal provider capability
recommendation.body: Keep the DeepSeek-specific behavior in provider or catalog metadata and avoid another public option unless a supported operator opt-out is required.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the canonical tail runtime-context behavior for the same prompt-cache stability boundary.
